title: Escal-Vigor
author: Georges Eekhoud
current_text: Georges Eekhoud was prosecuted in 1900 over the perceived salaciousness of Escal-Vigor and was acquitted of the charges.

sources.quote: This topic was controversial to such a degree, that the novel was considered a press offence against public decency and Eekhoud was summoned to appear in court, where a jury had to decide whether or not the author was guilty of immorality.
sources.title: Georges Eekhoud: the Belgian Maxim Gorki | Erfgoedbibliotheek Hendrik Conscience

sources.quote: In the end, Eekhoud was acquitted of the charges, but the fear of exposure and social ‘excommunication’ urged him to strongly deny accusations on being a homosexual himself.
sources.title: Georges Eekhoud: the Belgian Maxim Gorki | Erfgoedbibliotheek Hendrik Conscience

sources.quote: Much like his French decadent contemporary Rachilde with Monsieur Vénus (1884), Eekhoud was prosecuted in 1900 for the perceived salaciousness of Escal-Vigor, whose unapologetically positive depiction of male homosexual desire scandalised both the courts and salons.

ban_rows.note: One of the first European novels overtly defending homosexuality; prosecuted at Bruges in 1900 as pornography/an affront to morals. Eekhoud was acquitted after a writers' petition (a prosecution rather than a completed ban).
